elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause: "Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Harpoon shall ..." — both trigger events, any cause, covered.

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: Inserted (a) provides assistance "for a period of at least ninety (90) days"; no six-month period is stated. Repair by substituting "up to six (6) months".

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
elements.evidence: Inserted (a) says only "reasonable transition assistance"; no charging basis (then-current rates) appears anywhere in the new operative language.

elements.element: Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Inserted (b): "within thirty (30) days after such effective date, return to AbbVie all data and other Confidential Information of AbbVie in Harpoon's possession or Control", with the effective date being that of the expiration/termination.

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: Inserted (b) specifies no format; the agreement's retained Section 9.7 also specifies none. Repair by adding "in a commonly used, machine-readable format".

elements.element: Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: No deletion-and-certification step follows the return; Section 9.7(a) certification applies only to the alternative destruction election, which the new clause expressly overrides ("notwithstanding Section 9.7").

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: "Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason" — the 90-day assistance and 30-day return both run from the effective date of any such expiry or termination; the "at AbbVie's request" condition is available after every covered event, not only anticipated expiry.

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: "provide AbbVie with reasonable transition assistance for a period of at least ninety (90) days following the effective date of such expiration or termination".

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: "notwithstanding Section 9.7, within thirty (30) days after such effective date, return to AbbVie all data and other Confidential Information of AbbVie" — fixed 30-day deadline anchored to termination/expiry, displacing the request-based, destruction-electable 9.7 mechanic.

reasons: Position-complete at the fallback: all three fallback elements are met in operative language (any expiry/termination trigger, at least 90 days of assistance, 30-day return anchored to the effective date). Preferred is not reached (90 days rather than six months, no then-current-rate charging, no machine-readable format, no post-return deletion certificate).

Minimality defect 1 — over-broad override: a blanket "notwithstanding Section 9.7" is wider than the fallback checklist requires. Only the Section 9.7(a) destruction election and the "as soon as reasonably practicable" timing needed to be displaced; as drafted the override also strips Harpoon's retained one-copy proviso for continuing obligations, Applicable Law, litigation/archival purposes and automatic back-ups. Narrow it to "notwithstanding the destruction election and timing in Section 9.7(a)-(b)" (or "without limiting Section 9.7").

Minimality defect 2 — scope beyond the element: limb (b) requires return of "all data and other Confidential Information of AbbVie", extending the obligation past the Customer-Data export element to all AbbVie Confidential Information. Confine limb (b) to AbbVie's data (and Confidential Information constituting AbbVie data) unless a broader return is separately required.

Intent defect — contradiction with retained termination mechanics: limb (b) requires return of "all data ... of AbbVie in Harpoon's possession or Control" with no carve-out for information Harpoon retains rights to under the surviving provisions, so it collides with the Article 12 reversion regime (Sections 12.6-12.7) under which AbbVie data, know-how and regulatory materials pass to and are used by Harpoon post-termination. Repair by adding: "other than data and Confidential Information to which Harpoon retains rights under the surviving provisions of this Agreement, including Sections 12.6 and 12.7".

Drafting check — the inserted clause uses the capitalised term "Control" for physical data holdings; in this agreement "Control" is an IP/licensing concept. Confirm the defined term or replace with lower-case "control" to avoid an unintended or dangling defined-term reference.

No other retained language was deleted or paraphrased, and Sections 9.7 and 12.10.2 otherwise survive intact; the finding's "missing" classification is sound because no existing provision imposes wind-down assistance or a deadline-bound return on Harpoon.
